payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the requested source DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD is visibly white rather than black. Fail if that counterpart remains black or another nonwhite color, or the source target is visibly removed without a corresponding white replacement. Unknown if its correspondence or color genuinely cannot be determined. This condition assesses the requested color; whether the counterpart remains identifiable as a DVD is a separate required condition.
node.binding: Track the small dark, printed rectangular DVD item near the center of the source image using its position relative to the surrounding snow depressions and shadows. Inspect the white circular object occupying that location in the edited image. A changed outline or removed printing does not by itself make positional correspondence unknowable. Distinguish this candidate from the white disc at the location of the separate dark object on the right; that separate disc cannot satisfy this condition.

node_traces.evidence: The small printed rectangular DVD near the center of the source is replaced at the corresponding location in the edited image by a visibly white circular disc. The separate disc beside the dark object on the right is not the one assessed.

d2: The trace correctly binds the target to the central white circle and distinguishes it from the separate disc, but it stops at uncertainty, leaving the aggregate unresolved despite the reference being “no.” Keep the explicit rule that missing detail is not proof of lost identity; instead, make the decision criterion operational for the requested edit and rubric: distinguish evidence that the target changed from evidence that the requested DVD conversion is complete, and assess whether the central object visibly supports DVD identity using all available image detail. The source is a small printed rectangular item, while the edited counterpart is a smooth white circle with no discernible aperture or other diagnostic structure; do not infer DVD identity from whiteness or circular shape alone, but do not treat low resolution alone as evidence of failure either. Clarify how this identity check contributes to the aggregate completion judgment when evidence remains insufficient, rather than forcing a pass/fail label from the reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; this is a criterion/aggregation ambiguity, not a binding error.
